caption.verbatim: Figure1 Top 10 threats in the Emerging Cybersecurity Threats 2030 published by the EU

items.caption_verbatim: Figure1 Top 10 threats in the Emerging Cybersecurity Threats 2030 published by the EU
items.note: a hub-and-spoke infographic: one red central disc carrying a white telescope glyph and the label 'THREATS 2030', with ten spokes numbered 1-10 running out to icon discs for supply chain compromise, disinformation, digital surveillance, human error and legacy systems, smart-device data, space-based infrastructure, hybrid threats, skill shortage, cross-border ICT providers as single point of failure, and AI abuse. The art prints its own title block in pink and blue caps, 'TOP 10 EMERGING CYBER-SECURITY THREATS FOR 2030', and an ENISA / EUROPEAN UNION AGENCY FOR CYBERSECURITY lock-up in the lower left, so the exhibit is second-hand: the paper reproduces an agency poster and credits it nowhere in the prose. No axes, no ticks, no legend box, no colour bar, no value on any mark - the only numerals are the spoke ordinals. The caption is the paper's first printed figure caption and it is printed BELOW the art in the unspaced house style 'Figure1'

a closed-loop workflow diagram for the paper's own KDMF model, and the file's only uncaptioned figure box. Two left bars read 'task 1 / Data Collection, Preprocessing and Visualization' and 'task 2 / Policy Information Gathering'; from them a chain of process bars runs K-Means Clustering Analysis, Topic Analysis Based on LDA, Difference-in-Differences, Comparative Analysis, and a 'KDMF Model for Cybersecurity' lock-up with '>>>' marks; a right column carries 'Analysis of Calculation Results', a bracketed 'MIC Correlation Coefficient Analysis & Factor Analysis' block and 'task 3 / Collecting Demographic Data'. Centre is a yellow-outlined shield holding a three-way pie lettered TASK 1 / TASK 2 / TASK 3 around a white keyhole reading 'CYBER SECURITY', with a small blue padlock at its foot; gradients and drop shadows give the arrows and the shield a pseudo-3-D look, and a long curved return arrow closes the loop from 'Comparative Analysis' back to task 3. No axes, no legend, no colour bar, no numeral printed on any element other than the three task ordinals. It carries no number, no caption and no in-text citation: the only pointer to it is the sentence 'Our work mainly includes developing the KDMF model', which names the model the diagram draws without ever calling the diagram a figure

items.note: six word clouds in a 3x2 block, one per LDA theme, with no theme title printed over or under any of them: top row ENCRYPTION / ERASURE / RECTIFICATION / PERSONAL DATA / PENALTY (data-protection vocabulary), CYBERSECURITY / PROTECTION / OPERATOR / COMPLIANCE / CERTIFICATION (network-operator obligations), CYBERCRIME / MALWARE / PHISHING / SEIZURE / WARRANT (criminal legislation); bottom row MONITORING / RECOVERY / INCIDENT / PLAN (emergency response), BORDER / AUDIT / EXPORTER / CONSENT / RECIPIENT (cross-border flow), INFRASTRUCTURE / PROTECTION / MANAGEMENT / DETECTION (critical information infrastructure). Largest word per cloud: PENALTY, CYBERSECURITY, CYBERCRIME, MONITORING, BORDER, INFRASTRUCTURE. The vocabulary is the only key that ties a cloud to a theme - the reader has to match the words back to the six numbered policy themes in 5.2. One caption serves all six and it is printed BELOW the block, split across the bottoms of the last three clouds, unspaced 'Figure8'. No axes, no legend, no colour bar

note: 33 sheets, every one of them 612x792, and the running folio 'Page N of 33' matches the sheet index on every sheet that prints one. Ten figures and five tables survive measurement, plus 42 excluded regions. The caption machinery is far more orderly here than in the rest of the lane: every one of the seventeen numbered exhibits carries a printed caption - nine figure captions and five table captions in the text layer, plus Figure 3, Figure 4 and Table 1 on zero-text sheets - and the only uncaptioned art in the file is the unnumbered KDMF workflow on p4. The house style is split, not consistent: every figure caption is unspaced ('Figure1', 'Figure8', 'Figure10', 'Figure11'), four of the five table captions are spaced ('Table 2') and the fifth is not ('Table6'), so the same document prints two different conventions for the same object class. All nine printed figure captions sit BELOW their art and all five table captions sit ABOVE their grid - the one position rule the paper never breaks. The numbering runs 1-11 for figures and 1-6 for tables with no gap in the printed sequence, but the text layer can only see nine of the eleven figures and five of the six tables: Figure 3 and Figure 4 are printed on the zero-text sheet 8 and Table 1 on the zero-text sheet 5, so 'Figure5' on p9 is the first number after Figure 2 that a text-layer reader meets, and the file looks as if it skips from 2 to 5. The audit of the two zero-text sheets recovers them: sheet 5 carries '2 Assumptions and Justifications', '3 Notations' and 'Table 1 Notations used in this paper' (header 'Symbol | Description', eight data rows, three rules, no verticals, caption above), and sheet 8 carries 'Figure3 Where are cybercrimes successful, and where are they thwarted?' (two 3-D extruded bar panels over a world map, labelled 'The five lowest countries' and 'The five highest countries', with a detached green ramp 0 to 89 and values 96.1 Greece down to 85.71 Finland) and 'Figure4 Where are cybercrimes prosecuted?' (a flat choropleth with a vertical colour bar 5.66 to 20), both captions BELOW and both in the unspaced 'Figure3'/'Figure4' style - so those three are declared gaps rather than items here, because a pasted page image returns no region to measure. Section numbering is broken in the same way: the printed contents on the raster sheet 2 lists 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 9 and 10 with no section 8, and the body headings do the same, jumping from '7 Sensitivity Analysis' on p20 to '9 Model Evaluation and Further Discussion' on p22 - there is no section 8 anywhere in the file, and sections 2 and 3 exist only as printed headings on the raster sheet 5. Pointing is the weakest part of the paper's exhibit prose, and it fails in three distinct ways. First, no exhibit is ever cited by number: not one sentence in the text layer reads 'Figure N shows' or 'see Table N', and the caption lines are all a reader gets. Second, pointed at without a number: p21's 'with the change in beta, as shown in the figure below' is the file's only deictic pointer and it leaves Figure 10 to be identified by position alone. Third, never pointed at at all: Figures 3, 4, 7 and 11 and Tables 3 and 4 have no pointer of any kind beyond their own captions, and the closed-loop KDMF workflow on p4 - the one figure with no caption and no number - is referred to only by its model's name ('Our work mainly includes developing the KDMF model'), so the reader is never told that the thing above the paragraph is that model. Panel structure: Figure 2 is a genuine composite (world choropleth, radial bar chart and ten upright cylinders in one frame, with a horizontal colour bar 10.39-96.1 and a 'Created with Datawrapper' credit), Figure 5 repeats the recipe in magenta with the detector cutting its colour bar off as a separate region, Figure 6 is two side-by-side panels under one caption with its own axes misspelled 'Nuber of culsters(K)', and Figure 8 is six word clouds under one caption with no theme title on any of them. Three colour bars sit in the measurable art - the 10.39-96.1 ramp on Figure 2, the 0.0022-to-0 ramp on Figure 5 and the 'Cluster' ramp 0.00-2.00 on Figure 7 - with two more on the unmeasurable sheet 8 (Figures 3 and 4), so the paper's default way of encoding magnitude is a colour bar and it never keys one of them in a legend. Three exhibits print values on their marks: the ten cylinders of Figure 2 (96.1 down to 85.71), both panels of Figure 6 (0.41 to 0.33 above the silhouette bars, 248 to 56 above the elbow markers) and the six bars of Figure 9 (0.849 down to 0.3215). Figure 2 also carries the file's only pseudo-3-D rendering (the cylinder caps), matching the extruded bars of the unmeasurable Figure 3. Two figures are decorative rather than quantitative: the blue fan of Figure 11 has no axes, no numbers and no scale, and the six word clouds of Figure 8 encode frequency as type size without a key. Seven sheets are flat pasted rasters with no text layer, no images and no drawings - p2 (contents), p5 (Assumptions, Notations and Table 1), p6, p8 (Figures 3 and 4), p11, p18 and p31 - and they are the reason three printed exhibits and two printed section headings cannot be measured. Twelve identical watermark QR blocks are excluded at 693 paths in the box 450-590 by 717-787, and the fifth table is the copy-paste tell of the set: Table 5's time and interaction rows are glyph-for-glyph Table 4's. Finally the paper's arithmetic of exhibits is consistent - four tables for four regression themes plus a one-row factor table and a DID summary, eleven figures for a paper that promises a map, a clustering, a policy comparison and a sensitivity check - but the printed numbers and the printed pointers never meet.
